title: First Engineer Hire for Seed Startups: November 2026
summary: Explore a clear framework for hiring your first engineer, covering readiness, salary, equity, and interviews (November 2026).
body_markdown:
You’re ready to hire your first engineer, but salary, equity, and interview plans are still open questions. Knowing[how to hire first engineer](https://www.dover.com/) talent comes down to finding someone who can deliver independently, within a budget that leaves enough runway to reach your next milestone. Connecting the role’s scope to the full hiring cost, a focused technical assessment, and a manageable first release gives you a practical basis for the decision.


**TLDR:**


- Check your runway, ongoing engineering workload, and onboarding time before hiring full-time.
- Favor independent delivery and debugging skills over pedigree for your first engineer.
- Budget beyond salary for benefits, equipment, and recruiting. Explain equity dilution and vesting.
- Use one job-like coding exercise with a technical reviewer and clear rules for AI assistance.
- Plan onboarding around customer context, code access, and a small, reviewed product release.


## Hiring Readiness for Your First Engineer


Customer feedback is piling up while product fixes wait. Before hiring your first engineer, check whether:


- Engineering work extends beyond the current backlog.
- Runway after hiring costs supports the next milestone.
- Product priorities can guide weekly work.
- A founder has time for onboarding questions.


> A full-time hire fits ongoing engineering ownership.


If the work ends with a defined prototype and handoff, a contractor or development agency may suit that bounded scope.


## The Founding Engineer Role and Its Boundaries


A founding engineer writes code, learns from customers, and owns technical tradeoffs across an evolving codebase. Clarify the title’s authority.


Role Responsibility boundary


Founding engineer Hands-on delivery with few inherited conventions


CTO Technical strategy, architecture, and hiring ownership, usually with a larger equity stake


Senior or lead engineer Hands-on delivery and technical direction within a defined scope


Nontechnical founders who want someone to own unresolved product and technical strategy may be hiring a CTO instead of a founding engineer, which changes the scope, equity, and search.


## The Skills Your Seed-Stage Technical Hire Needs


Your seed-stage technical hire needs evidence of independent delivery, debugging unfamiliar failures, and clear communication. Ask what candidates cut from scope and how they weighed customer value against technical risk; pedigree reveals little about that judgment.


A versatile product engineer suits application work, which is one piece of[how to hire top engineers](https://www.dover.com/blog/how-to-hire-engineers-your-ultimate-guide) for a growing team. Seek specialist depth when security, infrastructure, hardware, or research drives the hardest problems.


A junior engineer needs regular code review and mentorship. Without that support, favor independent delivery over seniority labels.


## Salary, Equity, and a Sustainable Hiring Budget


Set salary by location, responsibility, experience, and runway. Budget separately for benefits, employer costs, equipment, and recruiting.


Broad reference Benchmark


O*NET’s[BLS 2025 developer wages](https://www.onetonline.org/link/localwages/15-1252.00) Approximately $105,000 to $172,000 annually for the middle half of U.S. software developers; local wages vary


SaaStr’s[Carta first-employee equity summary](https://www.saastr.com/how-much-equity-to-give-your-first-employees-the-real-data-from-50000-startups/) Median fully diluted equity: 1.50%


BLS[Employer Costs for Employee Compensation](https://www.bls.gov/news.release/ecec.nr0.htm) Benefits made up about 30% of private-industry employer compensation costs in June 2026, on top of wages


These aren’t founding-engineer offer recommendations; equity covers first employees across roles.


AI-heavy roles often pay considerably more than the general developer range above, as AI funding in 2025 and 2026 has pushed up offers for machine learning and AI infrastructure talent. If your first engineer needs that depth, budget above the general range and expect cash and equity to be negotiated together.


Explain vesting, dilution’s effect on ownership, and option exercise costs and deadlines, a topic covered further in this[guide to hiring engineers](https://www.dover.com/ebooks/how-to-hire-engineers) . Exercising options can carry tax consequences, and the IRS outlines[stock option tax treatment](https://www.irs.gov/taxtopics/tc427) for incentive and nonstatutory options. Equity has no guaranteed cash payout.


## A Job Description Built Around Real Ownership


For your first engineer hire, replace these brackets with concrete details:


- Customers need \[problem solved\]; the product is \[current state\].
- Initial deliverable: \[outcome\] by \[target\].
- Technical limits: \[legacy code or dependencies\].
- You decide \[scope\]; founders retain \[decisions\].
- Working arrangements: \[location, hours, collaboration\].
- Compensation: \[salary and equity ranges\].
- Required capabilities: \[day-one needs\]; learnable skills: \[tools\].


Describe the appeal of shaping an early product alongside changing priorities and limited support. Choose the title that matches the scope (founding engineer, senior or lead engineer, or CTO) and avoid promising a CTO title by default.


## Candidate Sourcing Through Networks, Inbound, and Outreach


- For your startup’s first engineer hire, ask former colleagues, founders, investors, and engineering communities for introductions. Make requests forwardable: “Who would you recommend for \[engineering work\]? Could you introduce us?”
- Use startup job boards, allowing time for screening. Build relationships at relevant meetups and publish substantive technical work.
- For narrow skill needs, research candidates before outreach: “Your \[project\] relates to our \[technical problem\]. You’d own \[scope\]. Open to talking?”


## Recruiting Support for a Founder-Led Search


- Founder-led sourcing keeps candidate conversations direct but takes founder time.
- Independent recruiters add sourcing or coordination capacity.
- Specialist recruiting agencies can provide access to niche talent.
- Development agencies deliver outsourced engineering work; employee recruitment is separate.


Before engaging support, agree on scope, fees, exclusivity, candidate ownership, communication frequency, and who retains candidate records afterward. Recruiters may expand search capacity; founders remain responsible for role definition, technical assessment, and the hiring decision.


An ATS is the system of record: it tracks candidates, interview stages, and feedback. It does not source engineers, run outreach, or screen applicants on your behalf; that work takes recruiting capacity, whether a founder’s or a recruiter’s. For one role with a warm network and a founder who has screening time, self-serve hiring with an ATS can be enough. When the skill set is narrow, founder hours are scarce, or several engineering roles are coming, a fractional recruiter or fractional recruiting agency can add sourcing and coordination capacity on top of that same ATS. Reviews from past hiring teams help you compare recruiters before committing. A shared pipeline gives the recruiter and the hiring team the same view of every candidate, which can reduce duplicate outreach and handoff gaps.


## A Focused Interview Process With Technical Oversight


Share interview stages, preparation, and assessment criteria upfront:


- Founder conversation: clarify motivation and role expectations.
- Detailed project review: have a technical reviewer probe past decisions.
- Practical assessment: assess work against agreed criteria.
- Mutual-fit discussion: discuss working compatibility.


Assign distinct questions, collect written feedback before debriefing, and skip redundant rounds, following a structured approach to[how to hire a software engineer](https://www.dover.com/blog/how-to-hire-a-software-engineer) .


Nontechnical founders should involve a trusted senior engineer or independent technical adviser in assessment design and evidence review, consistent with broader guidance on[how to interview candidates for a startup](https://www.dover.com/blog/how-to-interview-candidates-for-your-startup) , while retaining responsibility for product priorities and compatibility.


## Practical Assessments That Reveal Engineering Judgment


Use one bounded exercise resembling daily work: debugging an application or changing unfamiliar code, a practice worth weighing against the broader[roadmap for a startup’s first 5 hires](https://www.dover.com/blog/first-5-hires-seed-stage-startups) . Avoid stacking unpaid assignments. Assess:


- Questions that clarify unclear requirements.
- Reasoning behind implementation tradeoffs.
- Tests covering likely failures.
- Code another engineer could maintain.


Define permitted AI assistance beforehand. Ask candidates to verify and explain their output, including AI-generated code.


A paid trial is another option, with scope, confidentiality, and ownership terms agreed before work begins.


## Reference Checks and Evidence-Based Hiring Decisions


Score candidates against the role’s required outcomes. With candidate consent, ask references:


- “What did they personally own and deliver independently?”
- “How did they handle disagreement or a setback?”
- “What decision did they make with incomplete information?”


Request examples without confidential employer details, a step that fits within a broader approach to[how to hire as a seed startup](https://www.dover.com/blog/how-to-hire-as-a-seed-startup) . Distinguish missing evidence from concerns: unclear contributions warrant targeted follow-up without lowering the hiring bar; ownership that remains unverifiable or consistently dismissive communication warrants caution.


## An Offer Process That Supports Mutual Due Diligence


Align compensation expectations before the final stage, with an eye toward how early hires can[build a team of future founders](https://www.dover.com/blog/dovers-founding-engineer-on-how-to-help-build-a-team-of-future-founders) . Pair the written offer with product direction, available resources, runway context, reporting relationship, and technical decision boundaries.


Give candidates time to try the product and meet collaborators. Be clear about which terms are negotiable, without artificial deadlines. After acceptance, confirm paperwork, remaining conditions, and the start date.


## Onboarding Around Customers and an Initial Product Milestone


Before your first engineer starts, prepare customer context, repository and infrastructure access, deployment guidance, and security expectations. Agree on a bounded first product milestone, decision rights, and a feedback cadence.


Aim for a small, reviewed release with enough documentation for someone else to maintain it. Leave room for learning; a product rebuild or full engineering organization can wait until the work calls for it.

## FAQs


### Is a free ATS enough if your startup is hiring only its first engineer?


A free ATS can be enough if its included features cover your candidate tracking, careers page, and interview process needs. Check which features are included before relying on screening tools or candidate-feedback comparisons. Recruiter support is a separate hiring expense.


### Should you offer more than Carta’s first-employee equity benchmark if your engineer candidate wants a higher salary?


More equity can support negotiation, but it cannot resolve a candidate’s need for dependable cash income. Treat Carta’s cited 1.50% median as context, then discuss whether a package within your cash budget meets the candidate’s needs. If you consider increasing equity, review dilution, vesting, and option exercise terms before revising the offer.


### How do you move your first engineer search from a spreadsheet into an ATS without losing candidate context?


Transfer candidate records alongside their current stage, source, last contact, and next action. If the ATS supports CSV candidate uploads, check which fields transfer and add missing interview notes or outreach context separately. Cross-check the imported records against the spreadsheet before resuming outreach so candidates do not receive duplicate messages.


### How does a fractional recruiter work with your ATS during a first engineer search?


The ATS holds the pipeline; the recruiter supplies part-time capacity for sourcing, outreach, and screening coordination. When the recruiter works inside your existing ATS instead of a separate agency system, candidate status, outreach history, and interview feedback stay visible to the hiring team, and those records typically remain with your company after the engagement ends. Agree upfront on which stages the recruiter owns. Technical assessment and the final hiring decision usually stay with founders and a qualified engineer.


## Final Thoughts on Hiring Your First Engineer as a Seed-Stage Startup


Deciding[how to hire first engineer](https://www.dover.com/) talent works best when the role’s scope, the runway after hiring costs, the technical assessment, and a small reviewed first release all point at the same outcome. Founders at different stages weigh those pieces differently, and a nontechnical founder often gets more from outside technical judgment than from a longer interview loop. Dover is one option for the tooling side: a free ATS that keeps candidates, feedback, and outreach history in one pipeline, with fractional recruiters available inside that same system when sourcing time is the limit. Whichever route you take, product priorities and the hiring decision stay with the founders.
